The site selection argument (that engineers would choose locations with adequate cooling water) weakens considerably when the region is experiencing documented water scarcity and the project was abandoned.

[FACT] The site is located in Karapınar, Konya Province, in Turkey's Central Anatolian plateau - a semi-arid region within the endorheic Konya Closed Basin known for severe water scarcity and groundwater depletion. [UNKNOWN] No rivers, lakes, or reservoirs can be identified within feasible engineering distance (~10 km) of the site coordinates, though detailed hydrological mapping would be needed to confirm. [FACT] The Karapınar area has experienced significant sinkhole formation due to excessive groundwater extraction for irrigation, indicating aquifer stress. [INFERENCE] While dry cooling is technically feasible for SMRs, the combination of hot summers (>35°C) and high altitude (~1000m) would reduce efficiency significantly. [UNKNOWN] The cancelled 1000 MWe lignite plant must have planned some cooling solution, but without project documentation, the intended water source cannot be determined. [INFERENCE] The cancellation of the original project may have been related to water availability constraints, given the region's documented water crisis.

The threshold requires transmission infrastructure capable of exporting 462 MWe, typically requiring >= 220 kV connection. [FACT] The Konya Karapınar power station was planned as a 1000 MWe lignite plant by Elektrik Uretim AŞ (EÜAŞ), Turkey's state electricity generation company. [INFERENCE] A 1000 MWe thermal plant would have required substantial grid infrastructure, almost certainly 380 kV or 400 kV transmission lines given Turkey's grid standards for plants of this scale. [FACT] The site is located in Konya Province, which is connected to Turkey's national transmission grid operated by TEİAŞ. [INFERENCE] Even though the project was cancelled, the grid planning and infrastructure assessment for a 1000 MWe plant demonstrates that the location has adequate transmission capacity potential well above the 462 MWe SMR requirement. The estimated grid capacity of 1000+ MWe significantly exceeds the 462 MWe threshold, therefore the site passes this criterion.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Konya Karapınar power station is located in the Central Anatolian plateau, approximately 100 km southeast of Konya city. [INFERENCE] As a cancelled 1000 MWe lignite plant, it was likely planned with rail access for coal delivery, which is standard for large thermal plants in Turkey. [ESTIMATE] The nearest major highway (likely the D715 or connection to D300) is approximately 5-15 km away based on the rural location. [ESTIMATE] The nearest railway connection to the Turkish State Railways network is approximately 15-25 km, requiring connection to the Konya-Karaman line. [UNKNOWN] No navigable waterway exists in this inland, semi-arid region. The estimated road/rail distances of 15-25 km exceed the preferred 5 km threshold for heavy transport access, therefore triggering the avoidance criterion and warranting "caution" for further detailed transport route analysis.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum (nuclear island) with 72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint. [UNKNOWN] The site area for Konya Karapınar power station is not provided in the site data. [INFERENCE] Given the planned 1000 MWe lignite capacity, this would typically require 50-150 ha for a coal plant of this scale, suggesting adequate space for SMR conversion. [FACT] The site is located in the Karapınar district of Konya Province, a predominantly agricultural region with extensive flat terrain suitable for industrial development. [INFERENCE] Cancelled lignite projects in this region often had substantial land allocations due to low land costs and minimal competing land uses. However, without specific site area data or detailed land parcel information, I cannot definitively determine whether the 14 ha minimum threshold is met.

The threshold for population density avoidance is 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The site is located in Karapınar district, Konya Province, in the Central Anatolian steppe region of Turkey. [FACT] Karapınar town has approximately 45,000-50,000 inhabitants and is located roughly 8-12 km from the power station coordinates. [INFERENCE] The immediate 5 km radius around the site (37.614°N, 33.591°E) encompasses primarily rural/agricultural land with scattered small villages typical of this semi-arid steppe region. [ESTIMATE] Based on the rural character of the area and distance from Karapınar town center, the estimated population within 5 km is approximately 3,000-8,000 persons, yielding a density of roughly 40-100 persons/km² (well below the 1,000/km² threshold). The estimated density is significantly below the threshold, therefore the site passes this avoidance criterion.
